roots.context: We have been learning that every living thing is made of cells, and that new cells come only from living cells. Now we ask what that tells us about ourselves and the world.

deep_truth.truth: Milk with living curd set into curd, but milk with boiled curd stayed runny. New curd bacteria came only from living ones, never from the milk itself. So every cell alive today, yours too, comes from an unbroken chain of living cells. That chain goes back to the first cells, over 3.5 billion years ago.
deep_truth.habit: We call a baby, a sprout or a fresh bowl of curd 'new life'. Its cells are new, but none of them started from nothing. Each one split off from a living cell, in a line that has never broken.
deep_truth.evidence: In the curd bowls, only milk given living curd bacteria set. Boiled curd, with its bacteria killed, set nothing. Remak saw new cells form only when a cell split, and Pasteur showed that boiled broth stays free of microbes if nothing living gets in.

three.who_am_i: You began as one cell. All your trillions of cells came from it, by splitting again and again.
three.what_is_life: Life is made of cells, and every cell comes from a living cell. Your cells are the newest links in a chain that has never broken since the first cells.
three.what_is_this_world: The world is full of tiny lives we cannot see, in every drop of tank water and every spoon of curd.

roots.thread: Every cell in you came from a cell, and that one from another, back to the first cells at least 3.5 billion years ago. The curd in your kitchen, the neem tree outside and you are all branches of that one line. This line carried more than chemicals. It carried the sensing and choosing that every cell does, and your own awareness grew out of it.

teachings.teaching: Uddalaka asks his son Shvetaketu to break open a tiny banyan seed. 'What do you see?' 'Nothing at all.' 'From that subtle essence you cannot see, this whole great banyan tree grows.'
teachings.link: Shvetaketu saw nothing inside the banyan seed, yet the whole tree grows from it. Science finds that the tree is built of cells too small to see, each one made by another cell.

teachings.teaching: Jain thought says every living being has a jiva, a living soul, even beings with only one sense, the sense of touch, like plants.
teachings.link: Jain teachers said that a being with only the sense of touch is still a living soul. Science finds that a single cell, with no eyes or ears, still senses the chemicals and touches around it.

teachings.source: Aristotle, On the Soul (De Anima), Book II
teachings.teaching: Aristotle taught that every living thing has a 'soul', meaning a power of life. Plants have the power to feed and grow. Animals also have the power to sense.
teachings.link: Aristotle gave the power to sense only to animals. Cell scientists now find that a single bacterium senses food and swims towards it.

science.text: All living things are made of cells, and all cells come from earlier cells, going back to a shared first ancestor billions of years ago.
Single cells sense, choose and keep a short memory. Whether this is the beginning of thinking, or of awareness, is argued about.

other_view.who: The Charvaka school of ancient India, and many scientists today
other_view.view: A chain of cells is a chain of chemistry. What is passed down is matter and chemical instructions, nothing more. A cell's sensing is chemistry, not awareness, and awareness ends when the body ends. Many careful people hold this view.

practice.title: The city of you
practice.say: Let's sit still and close our eyes. Put one hand on your chest and feel your heart beating. Each beat is billions of heart cells squeezing together. Now breathe in slowly. That breath brings oxygen to trillions of your cells. Breathe out. Now just notice: you are one, and you are also a whole city of tiny lives. Sit with that for three breaths.

how_we_found_out.story: In 1838 and 1839, Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann said that plants and animals are made of cells. But where do new cells come from? Schwann thought they formed by themselves in a clear liquid inside the body, the way crystals form in salty water as it dries. Many scientists agreed with him. Robert Remak, a doctor in Berlin, was not sure. For years he watched cells in growing chick eggs and frog eggs under his microscope. Again and again, he saw a new cell appear only when a cell split in two. He never saw a cell form in the liquid. He published this in 1852. Three years later, Rudolf Virchow wrote the same idea as a famous Latin line, 'omnis cellula e cellula', which means every cell comes from a cell. Virchow became famous for it, and Remak was mostly forgotten. Part of the reason was that Remak was Jewish, and Prussian universities held Jewish scientists back. He was never made a full professor. Today historians give him the credit.
how_we_found_out.who: Robert Remak, who showed it, and Rudolf Virchow, who made it famous
how_we_found_out.wrong_idea: New cells form by themselves in a clear liquid, like crystals in drying salt water. Remak watched growing eggs for years and saw new cells appear only when a cell split.
